source.publication: 2025 PIT-RES Resident Individual Income Tax Return Instructions and Form PIT-RES 2025; tax rate schedule from 30 Del. C. §1102(a)(14)
source.section: Instructions PDF p.6 Line 6 Pension Exclusion (under-60 rules, 60-or-over worksheet lines 1-4, eligible retirement income, NOTE, example); Form PIT-RES p.1 Line 6 military pension box; Form PIT-RES Lines 1-12, 20a-24, 26-27b, 32-33; Instructions PDF p.5 Line 1; PDF p.8 Line 20a standard deduction table, Line 24, Line 27a; PDF p.9 Line 27b; tax rate schedule 30 Del. C. §1102(a)(14) (record brackets cite)

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (you) 30,050.00 + U.S. military pension (you) 14,000.00 + private pension (you) 3,000.00 = 47,050.00. Federal taxable income = 47,050.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 31,300.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form PIT-RES (filing status 1 single, Column B): Line 1 federal AGI 47,050.00; Line 2 other states' obligations interest 0.00; Line 3 0.00; Line 4 total 47,050.00. Line 5 U.S. obligations interest 0.00. Line 6 pension exclusion, you (age 52): one exclusion only (PDF p.6 NOTE: 'ONLY ONE pension exclusion, even if ... receiving more than one pension'); the better branch is the military one, lesser of 12,500.00 and the military pension 14,000.00 = 12,500.00 (the non-military branch would give lesser of 2,000.00 and 3,000.00 = 2,000.00; the two are not added, which would give 14,500.00) = 12,500.00. Line 7 0.00; Line 8a 0.00; Line 8b 0.00. Line 9 (Lines 5-8b) = 12,500.00. Line 10 = 47,050.00 - 12,500.00 = 34,550.00. Line 11 0.00 (Line 11 worksheet: under 60 and not disabled). Line 12 Delaware AGI = 34,550.00. Line 20a standard deduction (filing status 1) 3,250.00; Line 21 additional standard deduction 0 box(es) for 65 or over x 2,500.00 = 0.00; Line 22 = 3,250.00. Line 23 taxable income = 34,550.00 - 3,250.00 = 31,300.00. Line 24 tax, §1102(a)(14) schedule as numbers: 2.2% x 3,000.00 = 66.00 + 3.9% x 5,000.00 = 195.00 + 4.8% x 10,000.00 = 480.00 + 5.2% x 5,000.00 = 260.00 + 5.55% x 6,300.00 = 349.65; total 1,350.65 (the Division's tax table, not in the sources, would give a row figure; expected keeps the formula). Line 25 0.00; Line 26 = 1,350.65. Line 27a personal credits 1 x 110.00 = 110.00; Line 27b additional credits 0 box(es) for 60 or over x 110.00 = 0.00; Line 32 total non-refundable credits 110.00. Line 33 balance = 1,350.65 - 110.00 = 1,240.65. Reading the military branch's 'amount of your pension' as all pensions (17,000.00) gives the same 12,500.00 cap.
